meta.objective: Replace registry-dependent native learned skills with a readable user-level knowledge store, deterministic prompt-time injection, lexical search, and lossless cross-runtime migration.

in_scope: Equivalent Claude Code and Codex prompt-time knowledge behavior
Readable user-level project stores for Git and non-Git directories
Canonical skill-shaped records, lifecycle metadata, and a disposable index
Exact trigger matching with one primary injection and bounded secondary metadata
A 9,000-character core ceiling plus stricter host payload validation
Atomic registration, shared-store coordination, and session deduplication
Lexical search plus learn and recall workflow integration
Conservative migration of registry-allowlisted legacy knowledge
Capability-only SessionStart behavior and native learned-skill retirement
Install, doctor, uninstall, generation, packaging, and real-host verification
out_of_scope: Semantic, vector, embedding, QMD, local-model, or LLM-reranked matching
Automated contradiction detection, pruning, curation, lifecycle transitions, or quality scoring
Repository graduation and pull-request maintenance of knowledge
Automatic relocation or a relocation command for moved non-Git directories
Automatic repair, rewrite, split, or winner selection for ambiguous legacy records

out_of_bounds: Do not add semantic search, embeddings, QMD, a local model, or LLM reranking.
Do not add a daemon, database, SQLite store, filesystem watcher, or background service.
Do not add automated contradiction analysis, pruning, lifecycle transitions, usage scoring, or overnight curation.
Do not add a lifecycle or status CLI or UI.
Do not add repository graduation, commit automation, or pull-request workflows for knowledge.
Do not add output sharding, multi-hook payload splitting, or preview/file fallback as a delivery strategy.
Do not auto-merge, rewrite, split, delete, or choose between divergent or oversized legacy records.
Do not hand-edit generated `plugins/spectre-codex` files or introduce a second runtime implementation under `src/lib`.

requirements_trace.description: Claude Code and Codex provide equivalent automatic surfacing and visible notice behavior.
Canonical learned knowledge lives outside the repository and native skill discovery by default.
Project stores use readable paths with canonical-root identity, optional Git enrichment, worktree convergence, collision expansion, and manual recovery for moved non-Git stores.
Skill-shaped records enforce schema, lifecycle values, active-only automatic matching, and direct-edit-aware index freshness.
SessionStart contains only compact capability and search guidance.
Active declared triggers are matched deterministically without a model download.
The primary record is injected directly, secondary matches stay bounded, and the user sees an accurate concise notice.
Core records are at most 9,000 characters and registration rejects records that fail storage or host payload limits while allowing focused resources.
Applied `id@version` values deduplicate within a session and reset on startup, clear, or compact.
Users and agents can search the complete active corpus through a dependency-free human or JSON CLI.
Learn and recall use canonical search, resources, validation, and registration rather than generated recall/native learned-skill dispatch.
requirements_trace.source: task_context.md Selected Design: Learning, recall, and search

requirements_trace.description: Eligible legacy records migrate losslessly and idempotently while oversized, malformed, divergent, or conflicting inputs remain untouched and reported.
Successfully migrated records leave native discovery while grandfathered oversized Claude records are reported honestly.
requirements_trace.source: task_context.md Selected Design: Migration and lifecycle integration

requirements_trace.description: Shared-store writes are coordinated and atomic while prompt hooks remain fail-open under contention or corruption.
requirements_trace.source: task_context.md Hard stops and plan.md Atomic writes and concurrency

requirements_trace.description: Install, update, doctor, and uninstall integrate the resolver and preserve canonical and unresolved knowledge.
The Codex mirror remains generated and the packed artifact contains the complete canonical runtime.
Automated and real-host evidence proves inline delivery, parity, dedupe, reset, no-match silence, migration, and non-Git behavior.

where_this_fits: Canonical runtime logic is authored under `plugins/spectre/hooks/scripts/knowledge/`.
Claude and Codex hook scripts are thin adapters over the same dependency-free Node modules.
The Codex plugin under `plugins/spectre-codex` is generated by `npm run sync-codex`.
technical_approach: Build store identity, schema, index, locking, and payload gates before migrating user data.
Use registry rows only as a migration allowlist; never scan arbitrary native skills as learned knowledge.
Match exact normalized trigger phrases inside `UserPromptSubmit`, inject one full primary, and expose bounded secondary metadata.
Keep SessionStart constant-size and use it for capability guidance, dedupe reset, and idempotent migration.
Expose target-independent search/register/migrate commands and route npm-side integration to the canonical runtime.
key_decisions: Git enriches identity but never gates learning or search.
Moved non-Git directories allocate a new store and preserve the old store for manual recovery.
The index is disposable and direct edits are detected at prompt/search time.
The 9,000-character core ceiling is separate from stricter framed host payload validation.
Ambiguous or oversized legacy records remain untouched.
No new third-party package is introduced.
